Right 3

The right side answers the left

The thread becomes selectable and the right half says what that element actually requires. Click or arrow through it. This is the only one that needs new copy, and that copy is about regulatory requirements, so it needs the client to sign it off before launch.

The seven elements. Covered.

The Office of Inspector General defines what an effective compliance program requires. SHIELD delivers all seven.

What the element requires

Standards of conduct and the policies that put them into practice, written for your setting and acknowledged by the people they bind.

A named compliance officer with the authority to act, and a governing body that actually reviews what the officer reports.

Role appropriate training for everyone the rule touches, assigned on a schedule and recorded as it is completed.

A route for staff to raise a concern, including anonymously, and a documented policy that nobody is punished for using it.

Published consequences applied the same way every time, because a standard nobody enforces is not a standard.

Auditing against your own risk areas on a schedule, with the findings written down while they are still findings.

Investigating what surfaces, correcting it, and keeping the record of both, which is the part an investigator asks to see.

Right 4

The dead space turns into the point of the section. Somebody reading a list of seven obligations is exactly the person who wants to know where they stand, and right now the nearest way to ask is at the bottom of the page.

Ground A

Raised panel

The section lifts off the page as one lighter slab, hairlines top and bottom. The simplest way to say this is a distinct part of the argument.

One platform that runs your compliance program and watches your billing.

Healthcare Compliance Pros is a compliance and revenue integrity partner for healthcare providers. SHIELD runs the compliance program: policies, training, risk analysis and the documentation an investigator asks for. SENTRY watches the revenue side, benchmarking your claims every quarter against your specialty.

What most organizations run
  • A separate learning system
  • A policy tool
  • An incident tracker
  • A hotline vendor
  • A spreadsheet nobody owns
What you run instead

Your whole program, documented in one place.

One platform, one login, one completion view across every location, with dated records generated as your team works rather than assembled after the request arrives.

SHIELD runs it. SENTRY watches the revenue. People stand behind both.

Superseded, not crossed out
